detail: The key path is correct, but the rationale for distractor 8 is wrong: if a student drops the sign and takes b = 8, then a - b = 6 - 8 = -2, not 8. The choice 8 is really the value of -b (or |b|) reported instead of a - b.

fix.old: 8 drops the sign of b when dividing 24 by -3.
fix.new: 8 is the value of -b alone, reported without adding a.

detail: The rationale for 31.2 does not reproduce it: using a rate of 0.5 consistently gives 37.2 (from lighting) or 51.2 (from the 40-minute reading). 31.2 comes from using the correct initial height 25.6 with the wrong rate 0.5: (25.6 - 10)/0.5.

fix.old: 31.2 uses the rate 0.5 from dividing 7 by 14 instead of by 28;
fix.new: 31.2 divides the 15.6-centimeter drop from the initial height of 25.6 centimeters by a rate of 0.5 instead of 0.25 (from dividing 7 by 14 instead of by 28);

detail: The parenthetical 'A combination may use only one size of box.' can be read as a restriction (each combination must use a single size), which gives 2 instead of the keyed 6. The intended meaning is that one-size combinations count; the wording should say so. Marked minor because the permissive reading is the more natural one, but a careful student could defend 2.

fix.old: (A combination may use only one size of box.)
fix.new: (A combination that uses boxes of only one size counts as one of the combinations.)
